prompts.prompt: Use case: style-transfer / targeted background-only art edit. Image 1 is the EXACT EDIT TARGET, an existing Unity game background plate, 1774x887, panoramic 2:1. Image 2 is ONLY a style/intensity reference: use the pale watercolor treatment of its DISTANT WALL AND FOLIAGE, not its foreground objects. Return one edited background plate with exactly the composition, crop, aspect ratio and architectural registration of Image 1. Preserve every tree trunk, wall gap, left iron gate, columns, flower bed and door at its original location and size. NO characters, no new props, no rays, no platforms, no text. Edit only the finish: make this garden backdrop a softer, moderately lighter transparent watercolor wash with muted sage/olive foliage and dusty warm terracotta masonry, subtle paper grain, broad watery pigment transitions. Reduce busy dark ink edges and small high-frequency leaf/stone texture, soften distant edges gently, reduce contrast about 30%, reduce saturation about 20%, lift deep shadow moderately toward warm paper. Keep larger shapes and original sunlight/colour identity legible. The previous over-white/foggy version was rejected: do NOT bleach to white, erase forms, or cover with heavy fog; stay at the balanced pale backdrop intensity seen in image 2's distant wall. This is a rear scenery texture, not a foreground/gameplay layer. Maintain the original 2:1 frame. Preserve no generated framing or border.

Use case: style-transfer / targeted background-only art edit. Image 1 is the EXACT EDIT TARGET, existing Unity background plate for the interior cross section of an overturned terracotta flowerpot, 1774x887, 2:1. Image 2 is ONLY the watercolor pigment softness/intensity reference from the approved next level. Return one edited 2:1 background, same crop and exact positional registration. Keep the entire pot silhouette, thickness and shape of cut ceramic rim, central top drainage hole, small entrance at lower left, and buried brick drainage outlet at lower right EXACTLY where they are, the same size and contour. Keep all existing roots in place. Add NOTHING: no characters, no gameplay leaf, no rocks, no light rays, no animal, no extra openings, no labels. Change the distant interior backing into gentler pale watercolor: lower local contrast of tiny earth cracks, soften hanging distant rootlets and interior stone noise, mellow saturated dark-orange/brown into dusty terracotta, muted warm ochre and a little warm-paper grey, soft translucent washes and paper grain. Reduce interior contrast about 30%, saturation about 20%; lift the deep brown wall moderately, not into bright daylight. Keep the pot's rim and the three openings visibly defined, preserve the sheltered underground warm shade and relative illumination from the little top hole. The approved aesthetic is pale watercolor yet still readable, NOT white fog, overexposure, strong gaussian blur or flattened all-cream colors. Let the empty interior wall recede so separate foreground art will read cleanly. Original composition and 2:1 aspect are invariant.

Use case: style-transfer / exact-layout background repaint. Image 1 is the EXACT EDIT TARGET: a continuous extremely wide rear-wall texture for a Unity 2D drainage-channel level, original 2170x725 (~3:1). Image 2 ONLY shows the approved balanced pale watercolor treatment on DISTANT masonry and foliage. Output ONE continuous ~3:1 panoramic background matching Image 1's complete crop, every pillar centerline, arched recess, root arrangement and opening pixel registration. Especially preserve the small square optical aperture in the middle pier at ~54% width and ~30% height, and both far-left/far-right door openings, at original positions and sizes. Do not change number of arches or columns; do not move/resize architecture; no foreground platforms, no characters, no lanterns, bulbs, machinery, water, rays, typography or frames. Transform the existing intense dark rear backdrop into a quieter pale watercolor painting: soften small dark stone outlines and busy distant foliage/root detail, lower local contrast about 35%, reduce saturation about 25%, lift dark areas moderately into desaturated blue-grey/teal washes. Preserve the cool underground atmosphere and slightly warm ochre brick arches; do NOT turn the underground into a bright outdoor courtyard. Delicate diluted washes, organic watercolor granulation, soft blended edges, subtle paper texture with enough masonry shapes still visible. It needs to recede behind unchanged sharp foreground platforms and gold light. Avoid milky white fog, heavy out-of-focus smearing, flattened gray wash or new composition. Keep original long continuous aspect and full visible width.
